notes: One entry per trap, with a stable `id`; ids never change when wording changes.
`status` is the deduplication result: adopted, merged or rejected, always with a `reason`.
This catalogue is authored reference content, not a name vocabulary; the schema and expression catalogues remain the source of truth for every name.

traps.title: Wrong encoding type for the data
traps.symptom: A wrong scale, odd aggregations, or an arbitrary order.
traps.cause: `type` does not match the data: `nominal` on dates or `quantitative` on text.
traps.fix: Pick `type` from the data: `temporal` for dates, `ordinal` when order matters, `nominal` for categories and `quantitative` for measures.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers encoding type values; added as a new note.

traps.title: Field names with spaces or dots
traps.symptom: A parse error, or the field is read as a nested path.
traps.cause: `datum.field name` and `datum.a.b` are parsed as property accesses, not as one field name.
traps.fix: Use `datum['field name']` in an expression; in `field:` escape a dot as `"a\\.b"`.
traps.reason: The existing field-name note covered the escaping rule; the issue's symptom, cause and fix were merged into it.

traps.title: Tooltip as an object
traps.symptom: Only one field shows in the tooltip.
traps.cause: `tooltip: { field, title }` is one field definition; it does not become a list.
traps.reason: The existing tooltip note covered the array form; the issue's symptom and cause were merged into it.

traps.title: Transform in the wrong place
traps.symptom: A filter or aggregate is ignored.
traps.cause: `transform` is nested in `encoding`, which is not a channel; or it sits in one layer while the other layers are expected to see its result.
traps.fix: Put `transform` at the same level as `mark` and `encoding`. A transform in a layer applies to that layer only; put it in the parent view to share it.
traps.reason: The existing filter-transform note covered view-level and ordered transforms; the issue's layer case was merged into it. The issue's layer claim was corrected after measuring with Vega-Lite 6.4.3: a layer transform applies to that layer only.

traps.title: Layer without its own encoding
traps.symptom: A layer does not draw, or it takes the wrong channels.
traps.cause: The layer expects channels from a sibling layer instead of inheriting them from the parent.
traps.fix: Put shared channels in the parent `encoding`; put every other channel in each layer's own `encoding`.
traps.reason: The existing layers note covered marks and per-layer encoding; the issue's sibling-channel case was merged into it.

traps.title: Signal referenced before it is declared
traps.cause: An expression earlier in the spec reads a signal that is declared later.
traps.fix: Declare signals before the marks and data that read them.
traps.reason: The existing signals note covered signal declaration; its ordering case was expanded with the issue's text.

traps.title: `data('x')` reads a dataset declared later
traps.symptom: The spec compiles with no error and renders blank.
traps.cause: `data('x')` compiles even when `x` is further down in `data[]` (or is the dataset itself), but returns `null` while the reading dataset is computed; the `formula` throws and the dataset stays empty. Forward `source`, `lookup.from` and `indata()` do fail at compile time, so only this one is silent.
traps.fix: Declare the dataset being read before the dataset that reads it.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers the silent forward reference; added as a new note.

traps.title: `random()` in a transform moves the scene on every re-render
traps.symptom: Generated points jump on resize or on any re-run.
traps.cause: A transform re-evaluates whenever something it reads changes (a signal, a field or its input data, such as `width` after a resize), and `random()` has no seed, so every re-evaluation draws new values.
traps.fix: Derive positions from an index (`sequence` transform, `as: "i"`) with a deterministic function.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers unseeded randomness in a transform; added as a new note. The cause was corrected after measuring with Vega 6.4.0: a transform redraws when something it reads changes, not on every run.

traps.title: An "LCG" evaluated over the index draws diagonals
traps.symptom: A pseudo-random point field shows regular stripes.
traps.cause: `((i * a + b) % m) / m` over consecutive `i` is an arithmetic progression modulo `m`, not an iterated generator, so the points fall on a few lines.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers the index-LCG artefact; added as a new note.

traps.title: `bounds: "flush"` drops marks drawn at negative offsets from the cell size
traps.symptom: The next row's header overlaps the row above it. With `"full"` a mark at negative `y` counts toward the row height; with `"flush"` it is excluded and overlaps the previous row. Telltale sign: only the first row's header is fully visible.
traps.cause: The `flush` bounds ignore the part of a mark that extends past the cell's top or left edge.
traps.fix: Use `layout.bounds: "full"` when a mark draws at a negative offset from the cell, or move the mark inside the cell.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers layout bounds in groups; added as a new note.

traps.title: `bounds` and `offset` do not move a group with a header role
traps.symptom: Switching `bounds` changes nothing, and `offset.rowHeader` moves the group horizontally, never vertically.
traps.cause: A group with `role: "row-header"` (or another header role) is placed by the header logic, not by the grid bounds or the row-header offset.
traps.fix: Use `layout.padding.row` to create the space between rows. The layout sets the header group's own `y`, so a `y` in its `encode` is ignored; position the header's content with marks inside the group.
traps.reason: No existing draft note covers header roles in a layout; added as a new note. The fix was corrected after measuring with Vega 6.4.0: the layout ignores a header group's own `y`.
